about: Every place the upstream kernel patch calls into SUSFS, and what this module does about it. Sites come from kernel_patches/50_add_susfs_in_gki-*.patch on the stable branches. They are identical on all seven except where a row names a branch. status: implemented, lkm-different (same effect through a hook an LKM can have), ksu-side, not-applicable, declined (considered and deliberately not ported, the note says why), missing (a gap to port, the only status the drift report lists), unreviewed (not checked yet). evidence: static (read from the sources, no test yet) or tested.

reviewed.level: hook sites and ABI, plus the kernel_patches commits listed under triaged; older commit contents are not reviewed

sites.note: The LSM matches on the pinned inode pointer first, then on (dev, i_ino) for a different object with the same identity. The fallback now also checks i_generation: an inode number reclaimed by a new file after the original is unhashed (ihold keeps the old object but not its hash slot, so the number can be reissued) no longer matches. This is guarded on both generations being non-zero, so a filesystem that leaves i_generation at 0 keeps the old ino-only match.

sites.ours: KernelSU side: skips the KernelSU sucompat hook for a known non-su process, an optimisation of KernelSU's own hook
KernelSU side: same skip in execveat and faccessat
KernelSU side: picks which KernelSU exec hook runs until /data/media/0/Android exists. Needs a kthread and fsnotify watch, which this module does not run
susfs_kstat.c (statfs and fstatfs syscall wrappers, numbers kept when the rule is added)
sus_mount.c and susfs_kstat.c (the statfs wrappers climb to the first mount that is not marked with follow_up(), by id range or recorded identity)
susfs_kstat.c (fdinfo kretprobe on seq_show, matched by inode and device of the descriptor's file, bind mounts included)
susfs_kstat.c (the inotify line is rewritten in the fdinfo hook on seq_show, matched on the inode and device it prints)

sites.note: Dead code on every shipping kernel. inotify_fdinfo() runs this on file->f_path, the inotify instance file, which always lives on fs/anon_inodes.c's single anon_inode_mnt and never attaches to a namespace tree. So real_mount(file->f_path.mnt)->mnt_id is never in the KSU range the branch tests, and d_path() on it yields anon_inode:inotify, which kern_path() cannot resolve anyway. fdinfo prints the inode a watch names, not the instance file, and susfs_kstat.c already rewrites that (the row above). The only gap is a replacement-mount inode that no kstat rule covers, watched before a per-process unmount; resolving it needs a sleeping path lookup (follow_up()) that a seq_show return probe cannot do, so serving it would require a wrapper on every inotify_add_watch(2) call for an upstream-dead, race-only window. Not worth the hot-path cost, so the finding is recorded but not ported.

sites.upstream: fs/namespace.c do_listmount susfs_is_current_proc_umounted continue (gki-android16-6.12 and android17-6.18 only; 6.8+ syscall)
sites.ours: sus_mount.c (grab_requested_root kretprobe forces -ENOENT for a hidden reader's listmount whose mnt_parent_id is ours; __arm64_sys_listmount kretprobe compacts our ids out of the caller's array and lowers the count)
sites.note: Upstream adds a `continue` after the loop's is_path_reachable() check so the page fills with real mounts, but that loop is unreachable from a module on shipping GKI: do_listmount() is inlined on the one 6.12 build checked, and is_path_reachable() is only called from get_dominating_id(), so a probe on it never fires for a listing. What stays out of line on both builds is grab_requested_root(), called by listmount, statmount and the syscall wrappers. It runs before the parent lookup, so a hidden reader's listmount with one of our ids as mnt_parent_id gets -ENOENT, the same errno as an unknown parent (the id is read from a mirror of struct klistmount checked against nr_mnt_ids, so a racing thread cannot change it; both callers path_put() the root on every path). This deliberately widens past upstream, which does not hide the parent: leaving it open would be a one-call oracle. For enumeration, the wrapper's return probe re-reads the ids already copied to the caller and moves the kept ones down. Editing the result after the fact leaves three residuals, none of which upstream has: (1) a page entirely ours cannot be lowered to 0 without ending the walk, so it goes out as built (full_leak on a buffer of 1); (2) a shortened full page looks like end-of-list to a caller that stops on a short page, a presence signal (a caller that stops on <= 0 is unaffected); (3) the ids sit in the caller's array readable by a second thread until the slots past the lowered count are cleared (clear_user; a failure is tailfail). tools/test_review_findings.py runs the real function over every hidden-id position, and the smoke reads the whole buffer (lm_app_tail_hidden). Matching is by identity (sus_mount_uniq_has), covering mounts the id-range test misses. The hook fails open and logs; mount_stat shows the counters. Unvalidated: not built or booted, but the QEMU smoke asserts the probes and the lm_* facts.

sites.ours: sus_mount.c (grab_requested_root kretprobe forces -ENOENT for a hidden reader's statmount of one of our ids; __arm64_sys_statmount kretprobe as a fallback only when grab_requested_root cannot be probed)
sites.note: This deliberately widens past upstream, which does not hide statmount(2): hiding listmount while leaving statmount open would be a one-call oracle for any unique id a detector already holds. do_statmount() is inlined on both 6.12 Images checked, so the hook is grab_requested_root(), called after the mount is looked up. The id is read from struct kstatmount (the mirror is checked against buf/bufsize first), and -ENOENT there copies nothing out, same as an unknown id (6.18 adds kstatmount.idmap, mirrored under a version check). When grab_requested_root cannot be probed, the fallback is the wrapper's return probe, which re-reads the id from the user request and zeroes the buffer, though a thread rewriting the request can beat it. Unvalidated: not built or booted.

mnt_id_unique is not crafted. Upstream (7d91da2) sets it to atomic64_read(&mnt_id_ctr) + atomic64_inc_return(&sus_mnt_id_ctr) in its allocators, before the mount is inserted. This module marks mounts that already exist, and on 6.12+ ns->mounts is an rb-tree keyed on mnt_id_unique (mnt_add_to_ns(), fs/namespace.c 6.12:1139, 6.18:1092), so rewriting the key of a mount already in the tree would break mnt_find_id_at() for statmount, listmount paging and the /proc/mounts seq position. The mount keeps the id the kernel gave it at allocation, which is already in range with no gap; the earlier in-place craft (c71bdb0) is removed.

sites.ours: susfs_supercall.c (syscall table entry, kprobe on the reboot syscall when the table cannot be hooked)

sites.upstream: security/selinux/avc.c susfs_is_avc_log_spoofing_enabled, susfs_ksu_sid, susfs_priv_app_sid (avc log spoofing)

security/selinux/hooks.c, security/selinux/selinuxfs.c selinux_hide: ksu_selinux_hide_running, backup_sepolicy, my_setprocattr, my_security_* (an app is answered from the policy without KernelSU's rules)
sites.ours: KernelSU side: kernel/feature/selinux_hide.c ships in tiann/KernelSU, SukiSU-Ultra, BakaSU, KernelSU-Next and backslashxx (not in rsuntk, which is lkm:false) and hooks selinuxfs write_op and setprocattr itself at run time. susfs_selinux_hide.c resolves ksu_selinux_hide_running via kallsyms at load and reports it read-only on /proc/susfs_selinux_hide, so a caller (the WebUI) can tell native support from none without guessing
sites.note: Not ported: KernelSU's own kernel/selinux/rules.c shows selinux_hide answers from backup_sepolicy, a full ksu_dup_sepolicy() + isid load that KernelSU creates and frees itself, so an independent copy here would mean re-implementing and tracking every policy reload the host's KernelSU does. susfs_avc_spoof.c's AVC log spoof is a separate kprobe and does not overlap. When native_supported=0 this module has no override of its own, and the WebUI reports that state rather than offering a switch that would do nothing. susfs_selinux_ctx.c (a new layer, no upstream row) covers the app-facing write/validity-oracle surface instead, the only app-reachable SELinux surface since policy reads are MAC-blocked for apps. Its query node is a kretprobe that runs the real write_op before redacting, so a hidden type costs the same as a genuinely absent one (closing the reject-timing residual), then drops the staged answer so a readable context cannot contradict the -EINVAL; where that return point is unresolvable it falls back to a pre-reject kprobe. setprocattr stays a pre-reject, since running its body would commit the transition it hides.

sites.upstream: security/selinux/hooks.c, security/selinux/selinuxfs.c, security/selinux/ss/services.c susfs_selinux_setprocattr, susfs_selinux_lsm_setattr (gki-android16-6.12, the helper behind susfs_selinux_setprocattr), susfs_security_context_to_sid, susfs_security_context_to_sid_core, susfs_security_context_str_to_sid, susfs_string_to_context_struct, susfs_sel_write_context, susfs_sel_write_access, susfs_is_sus_type_rcu
sites.ours: susfs_selinux_ctx.c (kretprobe on selinux_transaction_write for the selinuxfs query nodes, kprobe on security_setprocattr)
sites.note: Upstream hides every type that KernelSU adds with ksu_type(), recorded by the kernel patch, and only while KernelSU's selinux_hide runs. Here the hidden types are a list the admin sets through /proc/susfs_selinux_ctx. It is empty by default, so no type is hidden until one is added. The answer to a hidden type is the -EINVAL an absent type gets, as upstream.

sites.ours: KernelSU side: the selinux_hide that the KernelSU forks ship answers access queries from backup_sepolicy, see the selinux_hide row. susfs_selinux_hide.c reports whether it runs
sites.note: Upstream records the allowed bits each ksu_allow() rule changes and restores them in an access query's answer; this module keeps no such record. Checked against KernelSU's own apply_kernelsu_rules(): every static allow rule it installs names a KSU type in scontext or tcontext, so a query that would reveal one already gets -EINVAL from susfs_selinux_ctx.c's type reject, a stronger answer than upstream's bit-reversion since the query fails outright. The only gap is a user-crafted stock-to-stock rule pushed at runtime through handle_sepolicy(), which would need a manual per-rule raw av bitmask to spoof and is not part of default KernelSU. Not built: the common case is already covered by the stronger reject, and the residual is not usefully configurable. Without a KernelSU-side selinux_hide, such a custom rule stays visible to a query.

sites.ours: susfs_selinux_status.c (kprobe pre_handler on both status-page writers, skipped whole for a KernelSU-origin caller)
sites.note: /sys/fs/selinux/status is a page apps mmap to detect a reload or an enforcing change by its sequence counter. KernelSU bumps it from reset_avc_cache() on every apply_kernelsu_rules() and manager handle_sepolicy(); upstream skips that bump for a ksu-domain write, since the AVC is reset separately by avc_ss_reset(), so skipping the status update changes nothing the kernel enforces. A kprobe pre_handler skips the whole selinux_status_update_*() call for a caller this file hides (susfs_probe_return()), and is version-agnostic since the handler reads no args. The gate has two halves. uid 0 is a direct secid compare against status_su_ctx (its own param, defaulting to "u:r:su:s0"), not KernelSU's own uid-0 predicate, which measured false for a real su-escalated setenforce on a gki-android16-6.12 Cuttlefish guest with KernelSU-Next despite the audit log showing subj=u:r:su:s0. Every other uid goes through susfs_ksu_allow_uid() (manager, per-profile su-granted uid), which is uid based and unaffected by that finding. Divergence from upstream: upstream keys both halves on one ksu-domain SID, this keys root on a locally resolved SID and the rest on KernelSU's allowlist. Limitation: the skip reads current at the writer, so a fork that deferred the status update to a kworker would run outside the originating context and go uncaught. Tested: the QEMU smoke proves both probes arm on every KMI and that a non-ksu reload still bumps the page; the Cuttlefish guest proves a su-origin setenforce leaves the page unchanged and raises the skip counter.

sites.upstream: security/selinux/ss/services.c susfs_is_current_ksu_domain (selinux_policy_commit, security_set_bools: leave latest_granting as it was)
sites.note: Not ported: no app-observable gain and no safe single-point hook. Upstream leaves latest_granting unchanged when KernelSU's own domain commits a policy or sets booleans, a counter internal to SELinux's AVC ordering that an app cannot read. The edit sits in the middle of selinux_policy_commit() and security_set_bools(), which an LKM cannot splice without skipping the whole function and dropping the real commit. The app-visible half of the same upstream predicate, the status page, is the one ported (the row above).

sites.upstream: drivers/input/input.c ksu_handle_input_handle_event, fs/read_write.c ksu_handle_sys_read (KernelSU manual hooks)

triaged.commit: KernelSU: Fix compiler error (8930474 on 12-5.10 through 6b60a30 on 6.12)
triaged.result: not applicable: touches only kernel_patches/KernelSU/10_enable_susfs_for_ksu.patch (a ksu_close_fd call in the KernelSU patch). The module does not apply that patch.

triaged.commit: kernel & Kernel: priority uid filter: Fix UAF bugs and worker not able to run (eb95da0 on 12-5.10 through 519c86c on 6.12)
triaged.result: not applicable, covered by design. Upstream keeps the uid bitmap and the app-strings list as two objects and was missing a synchronize_rcu() before freeing each. Here the bitmap is the only RCU-read object, published with rcu_assign_pointer() and freed with kfree_rcu() in prio_swap(); the list text is read only under prio_lock, so no reader can hold either past a free. The second half moves the refresh worker to run after KernelSU's track_throne(). The module has no such call to order against: prio_refresh() is queued by a kprobe on the packages.list rename, after PRIO_REFRESH_DELAY, and re-resolves the stored list itself.

triaged.commit: 8879282 SUS_MOUNT: allocate a KSU anonymous-bdev minor from a high range (get_anon_bdev / copy_mnt_ns CL_COPY_MNT_NS)
triaged.result: not ported, for two reasons. (1) Prerequisite conflicts with the event-driven-only rule: the whole hunk is gated on static_branch_unlikely(&susfs_is_sdcard_android_data_not_decrypted), a static key that upstream keeps TRUE until /sdcard decrypts, then disables from a delayed_work armed by an fsnotify group watching /data/media/0, code upstream itself says it borrowed from KernelSU's pkg_observer.c (fs/susfs.c). That is a kthread/fsnotify/timer mechanism this module does not implement and the project forbids; without the flag the branch never fires, so there is nothing to gate a port on. (2) Blast radius: get_anon_bdev runs for every anonymous superblock (overlayfs, fuse, tmpfs, nsfs, ...). Upstream pays nothing when the static key is off; a kprobe would add cost to every call system-wide, against the no-cpu-hogging constraint, for a window (first boot before FBE decryption) that is marginal. Recorded as a tracked divergence, not implemented.

triaged.commit: kernel: priority_uid_filter: Refactor uid parser (fc9b6ca on 12-5.10 through f0939fc on 6.12)
triaged.result: ported. susfs_priority_filter.c now looks the uid up in /data/system/packages.list (prio_read_packages(), prio_lookup()), which names every installed package, instead of reading the owner of /data/data/<package>. One deliberate difference: upstream now skips a package it cannot resolve or whose uid is out of range, while this module still refuses the command (ENOENT or EINVAL), so a typo or a system package is reported. Only the pass that follows a package change skips them.

triaged.commit: kernel: priority_uid_filter: Add extra flag O_NOATIME with filp_open() to avoid updating the inode atime (b0e4746 on 12-5.10 through 68f62fa on 6.12)
triaged.result: ported with the parser above. The one difference is a second open without O_NOATIME when the kernel answers EPERM, which it does for a caller that neither owns the file nor holds CAP_FOWNER, since this module reads the list as whoever sent the command.

triaged.commit: kernel & KernelSU: Make priority_uid_filter as new feature (aa61fe0 on 12-5.10 through 2557ea2 on 6.12)
triaged.result: ported in part. CONFIG_KSU_SUSFS_PRIORITY_UID_FILTER is now listed by CMD_SUSFS_SHOW_ENABLED_FEATURES while the priority_filter layer is armed. The compile-time switch and the Kconfig and KernelSU patch parts are not applicable, since the layer loads on its own and stays off when it fails.

triaged.commit: kernel & KernelSU: Refactor selinux_hide, experimental, partially done (61fc8b7 on 12-5.10, 8934afa on 15-6.6, 15890c6 on 16-6.12)
triaged.result: not ported as one piece. The refactor makes KernelSU's ksu_type() and ksu_allow() record what they add into lists inside the kernel, which needs the KernelSU patch that the module does not apply. Its parts are handled one by one. Hiding a type from the context validity check is done by susfs_selinux_ctx.c for a list the admin sets. Answering an access query without the rules KernelSU added is left to the selinux_hide that the KernelSU forks ship. Keeping the SELinux status page unchanged by KernelSU's own policy edits is done by susfs_selinux_status.c, see the susfs_is_current_ksu_domain row.

triaged.commit: kernel & KernelSU: Remove unused code (c3358dd on 12-5.10, not on 15-6.6 and 16-6.12)
triaged.result: not applicable: trims code that the selinux_hide refactor above added to the kernel patch and to the KernelSU patch.

triaged.commit: kernel: selinux_hide: Revert to the safer hash mechanism and full tuple comparison (3c8f72e on 12-5.10 through a8af3db on 6.12)
triaged.result: not applicable: changes the hash of the allowed-rule list in fs/susfs.c, which only the selinux_hide refactor uses. The module keeps no such list.

audits.target: linux 6.18 internals used by sus_mount.c (mnt_id_xa, __xa_alloc, __xa_erase, ns->mounts ordering)
audits.source: android.googlesource.com/kernel/common branch android17-6.18 (kernel 6.18.33), fetched file-by-file with tools/fetch_kernel_files.py: fs/namespace.c, lib/xarray.c, include/linux/xarray.h, include/linux/types.h, cross-checked against android16-6.12 (kernel 6.12.96) for the same files
checked: every id taken with __xa_alloc is released exactly once: by the kernel's own erase when a marked mount is freed, or by sus_mount_ida_release() for an unused or orphaned id
alloc and release use the same xarray and the same lock call, and both run in process context
a missing mnt_id_xa, __xa_alloc or __xa_erase leaves marking off and logs the name, so the feature does nothing instead of guessing
kallsyms and the loader's own extern are cross-checked and a mismatch is logged
the 6.12+ namespace_sem lookup is compiled for 6.18 too

xa_lock() flavour: mnt_id_xa is declared DEFINE_XARRAY_FLAGS(mnt_id_xa, XA_FLAGS_ALLOC) (fs/namespace.c:80), no XA_FLAGS_LOCK_IRQ/LOCK_BH; xa_lock()/xa_unlock() are unconditionally spin_lock()/spin_unlock() (include/linux/xarray.h:536-537), and the kernel's own mnt_alloc_id()/mnt_free_id() call the same plain xa_lock() on this xarray, so our matching plain xa_lock() in sus_mount_ida_alloc()/release() is correct, not a guess

__xa_alloc() with a NULL entry: __xa_alloc() substitutes XA_ZERO_ENTRY for a NULL entry (lib/xarray.c:1995-1996) and clears XA_FREE_MARK on the slot it stores into (line 2006), so a NULL-entry alloc is unambiguously taken; xa_erase() stores NULL back and xas_store() re-marks a NULL store free (lib/xarray.c:816-817), so sus_mount_ida_release() genuinely frees it. Also confirmed mnt_id_xa has no other reader in fs/namespace.c (no xa_load/xa_for_each on it), so a reserved slot holding XA_ZERO_ENTRY instead of a real struct mount * is never dereferenced by anything else
mnt_id_xa is static in 6.18 fs/namespace.c (line 80) and resolves via kallsyms the same as every other static data symbol this module reads (CONFIG_KALLSYMS_ALL)

ns->mounts is an rb-tree ordered by mnt_id_unique on both 6.12 (mnt_add_to_ns, fs/namespace.c:1139) and 6.18 (fs/namespace.c:1092), searched by mnt_find_id_at() for statmount, listmount paging and the /proc/mounts seq position; the module therefore never writes mnt_id_unique (the earlier in-place craft read mnt_id_ctr and rewrote the key of a mount already in the tree, and is removed) and only records the kernel's own value for the listmount/statmount filter

mnt_id_unique allocation range check: mnt_alloc_id() allocates with xa_limit_31b = XA_LIMIT(0, INT_MAX) (include/linux/xarray.h:239-251); our sus_mount_ida_alloc() allocates within [DEFAULT_KSU_MNT_ID, INT_MAX-1], a strict subset, so a marked mount's id is always one the kernel's own allocator could have produced

refactors.commit: ed8a832 Refactor spoofing logic of SUS_MOUNT, SUS_KSTAT and OPEN_REDIRECT
refactors.scope: on gki-android14-6.1 only (33 commits later), not in the 6.12 tip or the other stable branches, which still gate SUS_KSTAT/SUS_MAP/OPEN_REDIRECT on susfs_is_current_proc_umounted_app()

parts.kstat-gate-widening: 6.1 adds a (uid % 100000) >= 10000 predicate and uses it for SUS_KSTAT only (SUS_MAP and OPEN_REDIRECT keep umounted_app). not adopted: adopting it universally would diverge from the 6.12+ tips (7 of 8 KMIs) and widen kstat spoofing toward the manager and su-granted apps. Our gate stays susfs_is_current_proc_umounted_app(), matching 6.12+.
parts.hlist-bucket-and-layout: not applicable: upstream grows SUS_KSTAT_HLIST/OPEN_REDIRECT_HLIST to 14-bit buckets and reorders struct fields for cache locality. We store rules in arrays, not hlists.
parts.feature-independence: already satisfied: SUS_MOUNT, SUS_KSTAT and OPEN_REDIRECT are separate tables with separate gates here, so they already work independently and can combine.
parts.add-update-size-refresh: deliberate divergence: ed8a832 refreshes spoofed_size to the current inode size on update (is_update). Our update keeps the add-time snapshot by design (documented at the top of susfs_kstat.c): update re-points target_ino/target_dev and, for _full_clone, also spoofs the add-time nlink/size, so an app keeps seeing the ORIGINAL stat after the path is overlaid, the hiding behaviour the feature exists for. The default (non-full-clone) path never reads spoofed_size (SIZE not in KSTAT_AUTO_SPOOF), so the two agree there. Confirm the intended app-visible size with a behavioural test.
